page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual instance belonging to the High Clock Speed ecs.hfc5 server family. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The instance is configured with two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading, paired with 4.0 GB of memory to yield a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 22 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned. Given the dual-thread allocation on a single execution core, compute density remains limited.

Benchmark results demonstrate entry-tier performance profiles across standardized suites. In raw compute tests, the instance records a single-core stress-ng score of 1347.29 and a multi-core score of 1787.79, alongside a Geekbench 6 multi-core result of 1258.0. Memory throughput reaches 10.2 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 9.66 GB/sec for writes. Application-specific testing reveals Redis throughput of 1.77 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 1.4 GB/sec, reflecting modest overall throughput due to the constrained physical core count.

The ecs.hfc5.large configuration offers low absolute infrastructure expense for dedicated CPU execution, but delivers modest aggregate compute efficiency relative to modern multi-core alternatives. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, minor proxy routing, microservices, non-critical background automation, and small-footprint development environments.
